episodes.167602: A backdoor cold front that moved through eastern and central New Mexico on May 15, 2022, helped to usher in better low-level moisture compared to the exceptionally dry conditions the area had been used to for several weeks. Meanwhile, a shortwave trough tracked eastward across Arizona, helping to set the stage for afternoon thunderstorms across eastern New Mexico on May 16, 2022. As the atmosphere destabilized, elevated thunderstorms developed across the central high terrain before advancing eastward. With these elevated thunderstorms, severe winds were the primary threat, and reports of 60 mph thunderstorm wind gusts were received from both Raton and Clayton.
episodes.168163: An approaching short wave aloft along with increasing low level moisture allowed scattered thunderstorms to develop on the afternoon into the evening of the 16th across eastern New Mexico. This activity developed eastward, organizing into a ragged line of high based thunderstorms as it moved across the South Plains, then into the Rolling Plains during the evening and overnight hours. These thunderstorms produced widespread strong to severe winds as they accelerated eastward, along with blowing dust.
episodes.168443: A few strong storms developed over Converse and Niobrara Counties during the afternoon of the 17th. This included a left moving supercell that produced golf ball sized hail north of Manville, Wyoming.
episodes.168444: Multiple strong storms moved into the Nebraska Panhandle during the afternoon and early evening on the 17th. This included one severe storm that tracked from north of Scottsbluff southeast towards the I-80 corridor producing up to ping-pong ball sized hail. Numerous locations also received large accumulations of hail.
episodes.168670: A cloud line near the lower Florida Keys resulted in the formation of a pair of waterspouts south of Key West.
episodes.168678: Thunderstorms developed in the southern Nebraska Panhandle as well as southwestern Cherry county during the early evening hours of May 16th. As they tracked east, they became severe. Wind gusts to 65 MPH, ping pong sized hail and a couple of land spout tornadoes were reported.
episodes.169046: Severe thunderstorms developed across the area resulting in a few areas with tree damage.
episodes.169048: A several thunderstorm resulted in isolated tree damage in Horry County.
episodes.169257: First round of storms produced hail reports in northeast Nebraska in the early morning hours. A second round of storms produced hail reports in eastern Nebraska late in the evening.
episodes.169271: Storms developed along an instability gradient in Nebraska and moved into southern Iowa and northern Missouri. The bowing convective complex produced gusty winds and large hail in Taylor county.
episodes.169429: Cold front leads to strong to severe thunderstorms for portions of south central Nebraska during the evening of May 17th. The first thunderstorms of this event developed over southwest Furnas County between 4PM and 5PM CDT. The initial concern was the potential for landspouts, and at least two were reported in the area of Wilsonville and Beaver City. As is often the case with landspouts, these were very brief touchdowns, and no damage indicators could be found, so they were given an EFU, or unknown, rating. This initial setup for landspouts was fairly typical for this region in which steep low level lapse rates coincided with weak deep layer wind shear, weak low level convergence, and a weak surface front that provides abundant ambient surface vorticity. Eventually, between 5PM and 7PM, thunderstorms ���unzipped���, or developed further northeast in Kearney County, along the advancing cold front, which lead to upscale growth into a couple intense thunderstorm clusters. Large hail was the primary hazard with this activity, and for the most part ranged from quarter to golf ball size. However, up to 3 inch in diameter hail was reported in Harlan County. The thunderstorm clusters moved east and southeast, and eventually weakened and/or shifted in northern Kansas around 8PM CDT.||Another separate broken line of thunderstorms developed further north, from around Kearney to Columbus, between 9PM and 10PM. This activity persisted for a couple of hours before weakening. Once again, large hail was the primary threat, with penny to half dollar size hail reported in portions of Hall and Hamilton Counties.
episodes.169516: Isolated strong to severe thunderstorms occurred across the southeast plains in the evening, with strong outflow winds to 65 mph the main risk on this day.
episodes.169673: Scattered thunderstorms moved into western Oklahoma during the evening of the 17th producing isolated severe wind gusts. As storms decayed several heat bursts were also observed.
episodes.169705: Significant moisture in the lower levels of the atmosphere made its way up through eastern portions of New Mexico into west Texas. An upper level disturbance moved across the Southern Plains sparking some thunderstorms. These storms were more widespread south of the Texas Panhandle, however a few severe thunderstorms occurred across the Oklahoma and Texas Panhandles with strong winds being the main threat.
episodes.169706: A weak upper level disturbance combined with adequate moisture and instability to produce a few severe thunderstorms in the area.  Wind gust to 58 mph and quarter size hail where reported with a couple of these storms.
episodes.169708: Significant moisture in the lower levels of the atmosphere made its way up through eastern portions of New Mexico into west Texas. An upper level disturbance moved across the Southern Plains sparking some thunderstorms. These storms were more widespread south of the Texas Panhandle, however a few severe thunderstorms occurred across the Oklahoma and Texas Panhandles with strong winds being the main threat.
episodes.169720: A few severe storms brought produced gusts up to 60 mph in Phillips and Sedgwick counties.  A brief land spout touched down in an open field in Logan County.
episodes.169747: A shortwave moved across Wyoming and brought severe thunderstorms with strong wind gusts. The strongest storm moved across eastern Yellowstone Park. An 82 mph wind gust was reported that blew down several trees. Heavy rain caused an avalanche that closed the East Entrance of Yellowstone Park for several hours. Other strong storms occurred in southern Wyoming where wind gusts of 66 mph were reported at the Sweetwater County Airport and 59 mph at the Big Piney Airport.
episodes.169748: Severe thunderstorms developed across northern Wyoming on the afternoon on May 17th. The strongest storm brought quarter size hail to the north of Basin in Big Horn County. Another strong storm moved to the west of Casper and brought up to nickel size hail.
episodes.169983: A long-duration severe thunderstorm event affect Eastern NC during the afternoon, and lingered well into the evening hours. Numerous reports of wind damage occurred, along with a couple tornado reports, and some large hail.
episodes.170043: For the 6th consecutive day in a row, at least one severe thunderstorm developed locally. In this case, a weak/stalling frontal boundary began to lift northward across southeast Louisiana as a warm front. In doing so, the lower levels of the atmosphere warmed, which provided a mid level layer of unstable air. Although not many storms developed in this environment, one storm in Slidell was able to utilize that available instability.
episodes.170070: A weak cold front moved south across extreme Southwest Nebraska and Northwest Kansas during the afternoon hours on the 17th. As storms developed along the front, brief landspout tornadoes were reported in northern Decatur and Gove counties. These stayed mainly over fields, producing no damage. There were also reports of pea to quarter sized hail with the line of storms. The largest hail report was also located in Decatur County in the town of Jennings. During the evening, a line of storms moved east across the Colorado border eventually connecting with the earlier line of storms impacting areas along I-70 as far east as Beloit, Kansas. When the storms moved over Sherman County it produced up to 58 mph wind gusts.
episodes.170214: In the afternoon of May 17 a complex of severe thunderstorms moved through northern Missouri, bringing some minor wind damage and marginally severe hail. Later in the evening another convective complex moved into the the southern KC metro, causing some strong winds after sunset.
episodes.170326: A couple of thunderstorms moved out of the Oklahoma Panhandle to produce some 60mph wind gusts late in the evening towards midnight. Instability was weaker further north along with modest lapse rates and shear, but DCAPE values showed decent values to allow for outflows to push the severe thresholds into the CWA.
episodes.170327: A low level jet of over 30 kts coupled with ample low level moisture with dewpoints into the 50s to near 60 helped to aid for MLCAPE values over 2000 J/kg. As a result, 1-2 inch hail reports occurred mostly in the isolated cells but a couple wind gust reports later in the evening when storms became more clustered before becoming linear further northeast.
episodes.170357: A line of storms developed across the Texas south plains during the evening of the 16th and tracked into western north Texas where a severe wind gust was recorded.

A brief tornado or gustnado touchdown occurred along the 500 block of |Hyman Rd west of New Bern around 8:20 PM. A single family home had |almost 50% of its metal roof torn off and a metal carport was picked up |with debris tossed up to 150 yards to the east. Several large diameter |hard and softwood tree branches where broken with a few softwood tree |trunks snapped in the vicinity. North of the residence, damage to crops |and trees were generally in a southerly direction while at and south of |the residence damage was toward the east suggesting rotation. ||This same supercell thunderstorm tracked east-southeast into the town |of New Bern with many areas experiencing tree damage mainly to small|but also to some large diameter branches. Damage indicators suggest|straightline downburst winds outside of the initial weak tornado|touchdown. No additional damage to structures was seen nor reported to |emergency services during or prior to the survey of this thunderstorm.
